documents.title: Estratto tecnico Parmenide - richieste online
documents.text: Il portale cloud ProntoMedici riceve dal paziente richieste e prenotazioni online e le rende disponibili nel gestionale Parmenide. Il paziente si identifica con codice fiscale e codice univoco; il medico gestisce stati, notifiche e richieste dalla propria sezione.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico JMed - accessi, firma e dispositivi
documents.text: JMed dichiara livelli di accesso personalizzabili per direzione sanitaria, personale medico e amministrativo, sincronizzazione con software contabili, firma grafometrica, lettore smart card per la tessera sanitaria e connessione crittografata della cartella polispecialistica.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico JMed - API web
documents.text: La pagina ufficiale descrive nuove API per integrare il sito web del centro con JMed, inclusa la prenotazione online e la notifica del pagamento per aggiornare lo stato della fattura nel gestionale.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico JMed - firma e tablet
documents.text: JMed dichiara modelli digitali di consenso e informativa trasferibili su tablet al check-in; dopo la firma grafometrica i documenti vengono salvati nella sezione del piano attività del paziente.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico DBMedica - API, FHIR, firme e integrazioni
documents.text: DBMedica dichiara API complete per collegare CRM e contabilità, integrazione Worklist PACS FHIR verso ecografi, RM e TC, invio di referti firmati al FSE 2.0, firma grafometrica su tablet e FEQ per i medici. Dichiara inoltre sincronizzazione con portali esterni di prenotazione e sincronizzazione iCal con Google Calendar o Apple Calendar.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico GipoNext - integrazioni cliniche
documents.text: GipoNext dichiara integrazione con contabilità, radiologia, laboratorio e gestione delle attese; indica inoltre working list per apparecchiature radiologiche e integrazione con software di laboratorio.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico GipoNext - firma documenti
documents.text: GipoNext dichiara una funzione di firma dei pazienti basata su Samsung Galaxy Tab A e Samsung Knox per dematerializzare i moduli privacy; referti, fatture e consensi sono archiviati digitalmente.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico Sencare - aggiornamenti e canale condiviso
documents.text: Sencare dichiara aggiornamenti in tempo reale delle attività pianificate, un ambiente digitale di data management e reportistica e un canale condiviso con vista comune per operatori, strutture e familiari; indica app dedicate per i soggetti coinvolti.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico Sencare - verifica identità
documents.text: La pagina ufficiale dichiara che un sistema di verifica dell'identità protegge i dati dell'assistito dalla gestione da parte di terzi senza consenso; l'app è disponibile per assistiti, operatori e persone care.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico Zucchetti - app e lavoro offline
documents.text: L'app per l'assistenza domiciliare consente diario, parametri vitali, scale di valutazione e schede personalizzabili. La fonte dichiara timbratura con tag NFC o georeferenziazione e salvataggio delle timbrature anche senza rete.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico Zucchetti - telemonitoraggio e dispositivi
documents.text: Zucchetti Healthcare dichiara telemonitoraggio in tempo reale tramite dispositivi medici certificati, app per caregiver e paziente, portale per operatori, televisita e integrazione con dispositivi per parametri vitali, cadute, posizione e geofencing.

documents.title: Estratto tecnico ADIGest - tracciabilità e sistemi regionali
documents.text: ADIGest dichiara il calcolo automatico di tempi di intervento, spostamenti e durata delle prestazioni, con tracciabilità delle attività sul territorio. La pagina ufficiale dichiara inoltre il collegamento a sistemi regionali come EDOTTO.

claims.statement: Inferred: medium implementation complexity for a new product with a patient portal.
claims.methodology: Assessment for a new application, not vendor price; drivers are the cloud portal, patient identity flow, request state management and SMS/email notifications, without observed regulated device or multi-standard integration in the consulted source.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Official source documents the portal, authentication fields, request states and notifications.

claims.statement: Inferred: individual physicians, paediatricians and specialist outpatient practices with patient self-service needs.
claims.methodology: Derived from the official target wording and the patient-request workflow; this is a market-fit inference, not a supplier-reported market-size claim.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The page targets paediatricians and specialist outpatients and describes patient requests.

claims.statement: Inferred: low hardware moat.
claims.methodology: No proprietary terminal, biometric device or installed hardware dependency was observed in the consulted official page; the evidence points to browser, computer and smartphone access.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The module is usable from computer or smartphone and uses a web portal.

claims.statement: Inferred: high implementation complexity for a new product.
claims.methodology: Drivers are role-based access, graphometric signing on tablets, smart-card capture, website APIs for booking/payment and accounting synchronization; this assessment is for a new application, not price or product quality.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Official source declares roles, smart-card reader, graphometric signature and accounting synchronization.

claims.statement: Inferred: multi-user private outpatient clinics and specialist practices with administrative and clinical staff.
claims.methodology: Derived from the official product target and the separation of access levels for medical and administrative roles; not a claim about market share.
claims.evidence_excerpt: JMed is presented for poliambulatori and studi medici with role-specific access.

claims.statement: Inferred: medium hardware/process moat.
claims.methodology: The signing workflow depends on tablets and a smart-card reader, but the official evidence names general-purpose devices and does not document proprietary hardware, installation or a locked device ecosystem.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The signing process uses a tablet at patient check-in.

claims.statement: Inferred: very high implementation complexity for a new product.
claims.methodology: Drivers are developer APIs, FHIR/PACS worklists for diagnostic machines, FSE 2.0 submission, qualified and graphometric signatures, external booking portals and calendar synchronization; this is an implementation assessment, not a price estimate.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Official source declares APIs, FHIR worklists, FSE, signatures and external portals.

claims.statement: Inferred: private clinics, diagnostic centres and multi-resource outpatient practices with interoperability and paperless-document requirements.
claims.methodology: Derived from the official features for rooms, equipment, diagnostic worklists, clinical documents and external booking; not a vendor-reported market-size estimate.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The page covers diagnostic machines, clinical documents, signatures and clinic operations.

claims.statement: Inferred: medium hardware/process moat.
claims.methodology: Diagnostic-machine worklists and tablet signing can create workflow switching costs, but the source names interoperable equipment and does not establish proprietary hardware ownership or installation lock-in.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The source describes worklists to diagnostic machines and signatures on tablets.

claims.statement: Inferred: high implementation complexity for a new product.
claims.methodology: Drivers are radiology working lists, laboratory integration, cloud workflows and a tablet/Knox consent-signing flow; the assessment does not infer undocumented standards or APIs.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The official product page declares radiology and laboratory integrations; the document page declares tablet signing.

claims.statement: Inferred: multi-specialty medical centres and outpatient clinics that need centralized patient, scheduling and diagnostic workflows.
claims.methodology: Derived from the official positioning for medical centres and the declared radiology/laboratory integrations; not a claim about market share.
claims.evidence_excerpt: GipoNext is presented for medical centres and integrates radiology and laboratory systems.

claims.statement: Inferred: low hardware moat, with a medium workflow dependency for signing.
claims.methodology: The source names Samsung Galaxy Tab A and Samsung Knox, which are third-party general-purpose technologies; no proprietary device or installation network is evidenced.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Patient signing uses Samsung Galaxy Tab A and Samsung Knox.

claims.statement: Inferred: high implementation complexity for a new product.
claims.methodology: Drivers are distributed mobile roles, real-time shared updates, care-plan coordination, identity verification and reporting; no hardware or regulated interoperability is added to the assessment without evidence.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The official source declares real-time updates, a shared channel, apps and reporting.

claims.statement: Inferred: home-care providers, professional caregivers and families coordinating from small teams to large operator networks.
claims.methodology: Derived from the official audience segmentation and shared-care workflow; not a market-size or revenue estimate.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The source presents the product for structures, operators, families and assistiti.

claims.statement: Inferred: low hardware moat.
claims.methodology: The consulted official pages document mobile apps and identity verification but no proprietary terminal, wearable or field device.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The source describes an app and identity verification without declaring dedicated hardware.

claims.statement: Inferred: very high implementation complexity for a new product.
claims.methodology: Drivers are certified medical-device integration, real-time vital-sign telemetry, wearable fall/geofence events, operator portal, caregiver/patient apps and teleconsultation; this is not a price or quality assessment.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The source declares devices, telemetry, apps, portal, geofencing and televisits.

claims.statement: Inferred: cooperatives, RSA, private services and local authorities operating domiciliary and telehealth programmes.
claims.methodology: Derived from the official target market and the declared home-care and telemedicine workflows; not a market-size claim.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The official home-care page names cooperatives, RSA, private services and local authorities.

claims.statement: Inferred: medium hardware/process moat.
claims.methodology: Certified devices, wearable events and operational telemetry can increase switching costs through data and workflows, but the source describes integration with multiple devices and does not prove proprietary hardware ownership.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The page declares certified devices and a wearable connected to apps and portal.

claims.statement: Inferred: high implementation complexity for a new product.
claims.methodology: Drivers are field traceability, automatic time/travel calculations, mobile operational data and regional-system interoperability with EDOTTO; no undocumented API or standard is assumed.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The official page declares automatic calculations, territorial traceability and EDOTTO interoperability.

claims.statement: Inferred: integrated home-care providers and regional socio-healthcare operators needing field traceability and regional-system exchange.
claims.methodology: Derived from the official positioning for ADI and the EDOTTO connection; not a claim about adoption or market size.
claims.evidence_excerpt: ADIGest is presented for integrated domiciliary care and regional systems such as EDOTTO.

claims.statement: Inferred: low hardware moat.
claims.methodology: The consulted official page documents software field traceability and regional interoperability but no proprietary terminal, sensor or wearable dependency.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The page describes software-based field traceability and EDOTTO integration.

notes.text: Gap di evidenza, non assenza: nelle pagine ufficiali consultate non sono stati dichiarati API, HL7/FHIR, DICOM, SSO/MFA o modalità offline. Non vengono quindi registrati come supportati né come non supportati.
La pagina ufficiale descrive API per casi d'uso web ma non specifica REST, webhook, standard di autenticazione o schema dei payload; il bundle registra solo API generiche.
La fonte ufficiale dichiara FHIR nella sezione Worklist PACS, ma non dichiara esplicitamente DICOM; il bundle non promuove DICOM come evidenza.

La pagina GipoNext è stata riusata dalla cache del registry con hash e accesso precedente; la pagina documenti è stata verificata separatamente. Non viene inferito che Samsung Tab/Knox siano hardware proprietari di GipoNext.
Gap di evidenza, non assenza: le pagine ufficiali consultate non dichiarano API, HL7/FHIR, offline/sync o dispositivi hardware dedicati.

Le pagine ufficiali dichiarano dispositivi certificati, app, portale e telemonitoraggio, ma non espongono API, HL7/FHIR o un protocollo di interoperabilità; questi elementi non vengono aggiunti per inferenza.
La pagina canonica ufficiale dichiara EDOTTO e interoperabilità regionale ma non specifica API, HL7/FHIR, SSO/MFA o offline; il bundle conserva solo ciò che è esplicito.
